I am an editor at Shanghai-based news website [Sixth Tone](https://www.sixthtone.com), one of the few English-language news organisations focused on China.

For nearly a decade, I have worked with over 100 scholars globally, translating academic research into accessible knowledge. My own writings and editorial collaborations have informed the World Economic Forum, Nature, EY, and other public and private institutions.

Born in China, I never stop learning about my country and its interaction with the world, especially in East Asia. I am also interested in how individually rational decisions — financial, technological, and political — shape the collective trajectory of society.

I hold an LLB and a BA from Peking University, and an Master's from London School of Economics. In 2024, I obtained the Legal Professional Qualification granted by China’s Ministry of Justice.

My personal interests fall broadly across Go (a Chinese board game that inspired DeepMind’s AlphaGo), chess, science fiction, art, language learning, and darkroom photography.

[Write to me](mailto:yineng.cai@outlook.com) to discuss the future of the humanities, AI, ethnography for market research, and why Edward Said is still relevant in 2026.<br><br><br>

## **Selected Works**

[How Inherited Time Impacts the Lives of Young Chinese (2025)](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1017810)<br>I interviewed sociologist Cora Lingling Xu on one of the most powerful yet overlooked engines of inequality inheritance: time.

[Queen's Gambit: The Lowly Chinese Go Player Who Conquered the Sport (2024)](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1015504)<br>Meet Zhan Ying, the female Go player whose professional setbacks and resilience resonate with a generation of Chinese youth.

[On China's 'Color Codes' and Life After COVID-19 (2020)](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1005452)<br>A reflection on the tension between emergency-driven technology rollouts and their lasting social implications.

[Exhibition: The Past, Present, and Future of Chinese Fonts (2023)](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1013536)<br>How did generations of efforts by scientists and designers helped the Chinese language survive the digital age?

[Book:《我们从未中产过》(2024)](https://book.douban.com/subject/36501049/)<br>I translated anthropologist Hadas Weiss's monograph, *We Have Never Been Middle Class*, into Chinese.<br><br><br>
